title: Same words every time
statement: Give each taught word or concept one complete definition of its real meaning, not an incidental property, used word for word wherever it returns, keeping words taught together distinct.
detail: A rebuilt lesson keeps each word's definition identical, word for word, on its card, in every passage glossary and in the wrap, under a one-definition rule that a validator enforces, because definition drift makes the child re-learn the word each time. A research summary on intro videos says to use the same vocabulary for an idea already taught, and the curriculum's coherence guidance asks a reading lesson to stay consistent with how the subject app framed a topic: vocabulary, level of nuance and framing. The science misconception synthesis shows what loose wording costs: biology's "high-energy phosphate bonds" language contradicts the chemistry and re-teaches the misconception even to students who learned the chemistry correctly. The definition gives the word's real meaning, and the wording carries from card, glossary, narration, feedback and review to other lessons, units and courses, checked in code. Words taught together are kept distinct, with none inside another's definition.
against: Keeping the same words is not always the aim: sometimes testing whether students can transfer across surface variation is the point. The lesson engine glosses each word for the sense its own line uses (see 'Words that carry the knowledge'), so one fixed definition could be wrong where a word changes sense. whether taught words are distinct is not checked in code. One wording used everywhere spreads its errors too: one wrong definition sat on every visible passage of a lesson (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-inceptbench-2026-09-30/REGISTER.md`). The comparison needs stemming: "Without stemming, L5 *menacing* was a false positive." (`shadow/content-eval/SKILL.md`, lines 314-315). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/round-5/peter-pan-evidence-repairs-2026-09-10/glossary/VOCABULARY-CONSISTENCY-PROPOSAL.md`).
